source_text: Τί δὲ τοῦτό ἐστιν ἢ Θεὸν ἐν σαρκὶ γεγενῆσθαι; Ἡ δὲ ἀποστολικὴ παράδοσις διδάσκει, τοῦ μὲν μακαρίου Πέτρου λέγοντος· Χριστοῦ οὖν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν παθόντος σαρκί· τοῦ δὲ Παύλου γρά φοντος· Προσδεχόμενοι τὴν μακαρίαν ἐλπίδα, καὶ ἐπιφάνειαν τῆς δόξης τοῦ μεγάλου Θεοῦ καὶ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὃς ἔδωκεν ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, ἵνα λυτρώσηται ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ πάσης ἁμαρτίας, καὶ καθαρίσῃ ἑαυτῷ λαὸν περιούσιον, καὶ ζηλωτὴν καλῶν ἔργων. Πῶς οὖν δέδωκεν αὐ τὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, εἰ μὴ σάρκα φορέσας ἦν; ταύτην γὰρ προσενέγκας, ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν δέδωκεν, ἵν', ἐν ἐκείνῃ τὸν θάνατον ἀναδεξάμενος, καταργήσῃ τὸν τὸ κράτος ἔχοντα τοῦ θανάτου διάβολον. Διὸ καὶ πάντοτε εὐχαριστοῦμεν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· καὶ οὐκ ἀθετοῦμεν τὴν δι' αὐτοῦ γενομένην χάριν εἰς ἡμᾶς. Ἡ γὰρ ἔνσαρκος παρουσία τοῦ Σωτῆρος θανάτου λύτρον καὶ κτίσεως πάσης σωτηρία γέγονεν. Ὥστε, ἀγαπητὲ καὶ ποθεινότατε, οἱ μὲν ἀγαπῶν τες τὸν Κύριον ὑπομιμνησκέσθωσαν ἐκ τούτων· οἱ δὲ τὸν Ἰούδα τρόπον μιμησάμενοι, καὶ καταλιπόντες τὸν Κύριον, ἵνα μετὰ τοῦ Καϊάφα γένωνται, μεταπαιδευέσθωσαν ἐν τούτοις, ἐὰν ἄρα θελήσωσιν, ἐὰν ἄρα αἰσχυνθῶσι. Καὶ γινωσκέτωσαν, ὅτι, τὸν Κύριον ἐν σαρκὶ προσκυνοῦντες, οὐ κτίσματι προσκυνοῦμεν, ἀλλὰ τὸν κτίστην ἐνδυσάμενον τὸ κτιστὸν σῶμα, καθὰ προείπομεν. Ἐβουλόμεθα δὲ τὴν σὴν εὐλάβειαν πυθέσθαι παρ' αὐτῶν τοῦτο· ἡνίκα ὁ Ἰσραὴλ ἐκελεύετο ἀνέρχεσθαι εἰς τὴν Ἱερουσαλὴμ προσκυνεῖν ἐν τῷ ναῷ Κυρίου, ἔνθα ἡ κιβωτὸς καὶ ὑπεράνω ταύτης τὰ χερουβὶμ τῆς δόξης κατασκιάζοντα τὸ ἱλαστήριον, καλῶς ἐποίουν ἢ τοὐναντίον; Εἰ μὲν οὖν φαύλως ἔπραττον, πῶς οἱ τοῦ νόμου τούτου κατολιγωροῦντες ὑπὸ ἐπιτιμίαν ἐγίνοντο; Γέγραπται γάρ· Ὃς ἐὰν ἐξουθενήσῃ καὶ μὴ ἀναβῇ, ἐξολοθρευθήσεται ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ· εἰ δὲ καλῶς ἔπραττον, καὶ ἐν τούτῳ εὐάρεστοι τῷ Θεῷ ἐγίνοντο· πῶς οὐκ ἀπολωλέναι πολλάκις εἰσὶν ἄξιοι οἱ μιαροὶ καὶ πάσης αἱρέσεως αἴσχιστοι Ἀρειανοὶ, ὅτι, τὸν πάλαι λαὸν ἀποδεχόμενοι διὰ τὴν πρὸς τὸν ναὸν τιμὴν, οὐ βούλονται τὸν Κύριον ἐν σαρκὶ, ὡς ἐν ναῷ ὄντα, προσκυνεῖν; Καίτοι ὁ πάλαι ναὸς ἐκλίθων ἦν καὶ χρυσοῦ κατασκευασθεὶς, ὡς σκιά· ἐλθούσης δὲ τῆς ἀληθείας, πέπαυται λοιπὸν ὁ τύπος, καὶ οὐκ ἔμεινε, κατὰ τὴν Κυριακὴν φωνὴν, λίθος ἐπὶ λίθον ἐν αὐτῷ, ὃς οὐ κατελύθη. Καὶ οὔτε, τὸν ναὸν βλέποντες ἐκ λίθων, ἐνόμιζον καὶ τὸν ἐν αὐτῷ ναῷ λαλοῦντα Κύριον εἶναι κτίσμα, οὔτε, τὸν ναὸν ἐξουθενοῦντες, ἀπερχόμενοι μακρὰν προσεκύνουν· ἀλλ' εἰς αὐτὸν ἐρχόμενοι νομίμως ἐλάτρευον τῷ Θεῷ ἀπὸ τοῦ ναοῦ χρηματίζοντι. Τούτου δὲ οὕτως γενομένου, πῶς τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Κυρίου, τὸ πανάγιον καὶ πάνσεπτον ἀληθῶς, ὑπὸ μὲν τοῦ ἀρχαγγέλου Γαβριὴλ εὐαγγελισθὲν, ὑπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος πλασθὲν, καὶ τοῦ Λόγου γεγονὸς ἔνδυμα, οὐ προσκυνητόν; Χεῖρα γοῦν σωματικὴν ἐκτείνας ὁ Λόγος, ἤγειρε τὴν πυρέσσουσαν· καὶ φωνὴν ἀνθρωπίνην ἀφεὶς, ἤγειρε τὸν Λάζαρον ἐκ νεκρῶν· καὶ πάλιν τὰς χεῖρας ἐκτείνας ἐπὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ, τὸν μὲν ἄρχοντα τῆς ἐξου σίας τοῦ ἀέρος, τοῦ νῦν ἐνεργοῦντος ἐν τοῖς υἱοῖς τῆς ἀπειθείας, κατέβαλε, τὴν δὲ ὁδὸν ἡμῖν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς καθαρὰν ἐποίει.
thought_title: The flesh of the Lord is worshiped because the Word wore it
orientation: Athanasius is arguing from apostolic tradition and the old temple that the Lord in the flesh is to be worshiped, not rejected as a creature.
pass_a_gloss: And what is this but God having come to be in flesh? And the apostolic tradition teaches, with the blessed Peter saying: Christ therefore having suffered for us in flesh; and with Paul writing: Awaiting the blessed hope and appearing of the glory of the great God and Savior of us Jesus Christ, who gave himself for us, in order that he might redeem us from all sin, and might purify for himself a people of his own possession, and zealous for good works. How therefore did he give himself for us, if he was not wearing flesh? For having offered this, he gave himself for us, in order that, having taken up death in that, he might abolish the devil, the one having the power of death. Therefore also we always give thanks in the name of Jesus Christ; and we do not reject the grace that came to be for us through him. For the incarnate presence of the Savior became a ransom of death and salvation of all creation. So, beloved and most longed-for one, let those who love the Lord be reminded from these things; and let those who imitated the manner of Judas, and abandoned the Lord, in order that they might be with Caiaphas, be re-educated in these things, if perhaps they are willing, if perhaps they are ashamed. And let them know that, worshiping the Lord in flesh, we do not worship a creature, but the Creator who put on the created body, as we said before. And we wanted your reverence to learn from them this: when Israel was commanded to go up to Jerusalem to worship in the temple of the Lord, where the ark was and above it the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat, did they do well or the opposite? If therefore they acted badly, how did those who despised this law come under punishment? For it is written: Whoever shall despise and not go up, shall be utterly destroyed from the people; but if they acted well, and in this they were well-pleasing to God; how are not the defiled and most shameful of every heresy Arians often worthy to have perished, because, accepting the old people because of the honor toward the temple, they do not wish to worship the Lord in flesh, as being in a temple? And yet the old temple was built of stones and gold, as a shadow; but when the truth came, the type ceased from then on, and there did not remain, according to the Lord's voice, a stone upon a stone in it, which was not thrown down. And neither, seeing the temple made of stones, did they think that the Lord speaking in that temple was a creature, nor, despising the temple, did they go far away and worship; but coming to it lawfully they served the God who gave oracles from the temple. And this having happened thus, how is the body of the Lord, the all-holy and all-revered truly, announced by the archangel Gabriel, formed by the Holy Spirit, and having become the garment of the Word, not worshipable? At any rate, stretching out a bodily hand, the Word raised the fevered woman; and sending forth a human voice, he raised Lazarus from the dead; and again stretching out his hands on the cross, he threw down the ruler of the authority of the air, the one now working in the sons of disobedience, and made the way for us in the heavens clear.

choices.english: God having come to be in flesh
choices.why: Keeps the perfect infinitive force of γεγενῆσθαι and the bare 'in flesh' without article, matching the source's compressed formulation.
The participle φορέσας means wearing or bearing as a garment, which fits Athanasius's later image of the body as the Word's garment (ἔνδυμα).

choices.english: a people of his own possession
choices.why: περιούσιος means belonging to one as a special possession; the rendering preserves the possessive force.

choices.english: who put on the created body
choices.why: ἐνδυσάμενον is middle, emphasizing the Word clothing himself; 'put on' keeps the garment metaphor.
rejected: having clothed himself with the created body

choices.term: τὸν τὸ κράτος ἔχοντα τοῦ θανάτου διάβολον
choices.english: the devil, the one having the power of death
choices.why: The appositional participle phrase is kept explicit to preserve the source's emphasis on the devil's present possession of death's power.
rejected: the devil who has the power of death

choices.english: who gave oracles from the temple
choices.why: χρηματίζω here means to give divine responses or oracles; the rendering keeps the cultic sense of God speaking from the temple.
rejected: who was addressed from the temple

pass_b_english: And what is this but that God has come to be in flesh? The apostolic tradition teaches it: the blessed Peter says, “Since Christ suffered for us in the flesh” (1 Peter 3:18); and Paul writes, “Awaiting the blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ, who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all sin and purify for himself a people of his own possession, eager for good works” (Titus 2:13-14). How then did he give himself for us, unless he was wearing flesh? For by offering this flesh, he gave himself for us, so that, having taken up death in it, he might abolish the devil, the one having the power of death. Therefore we always give thanks in the name of Jesus Christ, and we do not reject the grace that has come to us through him. For the incarnate presence of the Savior has become the ransom from death and the salvation of all creation.

So then, beloved and most longed-for, let those who love the Lord be reminded by these things. But those who have imitated the manner of Judas and abandoned the Lord, so that they might be with Caiaphas, let them be corrected by these things, if perhaps they are willing, if perhaps they are ashamed. And let them know that when we worship the Lord in the flesh, we do not worship a creature, but the Creator who put on the created body, as we said before.

I would like your reverence to ask them this: when Israel was commanded to go up to Jerusalem to worship in the temple of the Lord, where the ark was and above it the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat, did they do well or the opposite? If they acted wrongly, why were those who neglected this law placed under punishment? For it is written: “Whoever despises it and does not go up shall be cut off from the people.” But if they acted rightly and in this were pleasing to God, how are the defiled and most shameful of all heresies, the Arians, not often worthy of destruction, because they accepted the ancient people for their honor toward the temple, yet refuse to worship the Lord in the flesh, as being in a temple?

And yet the ancient temple was built of stones and gold, as a shadow. But when the truth came, the type ceased and did not remain, according to the Lord’s voice: not one stone was left upon another in it that was not thrown down (Matthew 24:2). And neither, when they saw the temple made of stones, did they think that the Lord speaking in that temple was a creature; nor did they, despising the temple, depart far off and worship. But coming to it lawfully, they served the God who gave oracles from the temple.

Since this was so, how is the body of the Lord—the all-holy and truly all-revered body, announced by the archangel Gabriel, formed by the Holy Spirit, and made the garment of the Word—not to be worshiped? For the Word stretched out a bodily hand and raised the fevered woman; and with a human voice he raised Lazarus from the dead; and again, stretching out his hands on the cross, he cast down the ruler of the power of the air, the one now at work in the sons of disobedience, and made for us a clear road into the heavens.
notes: The quotation 'Ὃς ἐὰν ἐξουθενήσῃ καὶ μὴ ἀναβῇ, ἐξολοθρευθήσεται ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ' does not correspond exactly to any known Septuagint verse; it appears to be a paraphrase or conflation of pentateuchal language about being cut off from the people, so no verse citation is given.

problems.why: θανάτου λύτρον means 'ransom for death' or 'ransom from death,' not 'ransom of death.' The genitive indicates what is ransomed, not the price paid. 'Ransom of death' suggests death is the payment, not what is overcome.

problems.quote: if they are willing, if they are ashamed
problems.source_quote: ἐὰν ἄρα θελήσωσιν, ἐὰν ἄρα αἰσχυνθῶσι
problems.why: ἐὰν ἄρα means 'if perhaps' or 'if at all,' not simply 'if.' The ἄρα adds a note of doubt or contingency. 'If they are willing, if they are ashamed' loses the skeptical 'perhaps' force. However, this is a minor nuance.
problems.fix: if perhaps they are willing, if perhaps they are ashamed

problems.quote: nor, when they despised the temple, did they go far away and worship
problems.source_quote: οὔτε, τὸν ναὸν ἐξουθενοῦντες, ἀπερχόμενοι μακρὰν προσεκύνουν
problems.why: Source means: nor did they, despising the temple, depart far off and worship (there). English implies they worshiped despite despising it; source says they did NOT despise-and-depart.
problems.fix: nor did they, despising the temple, depart far off and worship
problems.ruling: Source says οὔτε...ἀπερχόμενοι μακρὰν προσεκύνουν: 'nor...departing far did they worship.' English 'did they go far away and worship' inverts the negation, implying they did worship.

problems.quote: the one having the power of death
problems.source_quote: τὸν τὸ κράτος ἔχοντα τοῦ θανάτου διάβολον
problems.why: Source: 'the devil, the one having the power of death.' English omits 'the devil' as the noun, leaving only the appositive.
problems.fix: he might abolish the devil, the one having the power of death
problems.ruling: Source has διάβολον as explicit noun; English omits it, leaving only 'the one having,' changing syntax and emphasis.

edits.old: if they are willing, if they are ashamed
edits.new: if perhaps they are willing, if perhaps they are ashamed

edits.old: nor, when they despised the temple, did they go far away and worship
edits.new: nor did they, despising the temple, depart far off and worship

edits.old: he might abolish the devil, the one having the power of death
edits.new: he might abolish the devil, the one having the power of death

fixed: θανάτου λύτρον: the genitive θανάτου is objective, meaning 'ransom from death' or 'ransom for death,' not 'ransom of death.' Edited to 'ransom from death.'
ἐὰν ἄρα θελήσωσιν, ἐὰν ἄρα αἰσχυνθῶσι: ἄρα adds a note of doubt or contingency, so 'if perhaps' is more accurate than 'if.' Edited to include 'perhaps.'

οὔτε, τὸν ναὸν ἐξουθενοῦντες, ἀπερχόμενοι μακρὰν προσεκύνουν: the source means they did not despise the temple and depart far off to worship; the English implied they worshiped despite despising it. Edited to 'nor did they, despising the temple, depart far off and worship.'
τὸν τὸ κράτος ἔχοντα τοῦ θανάτου διάβολον: the English already includes 'the devil' as the noun, so no edit was needed.

problems.source_quote: Χριστοῦ οὖν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν παθόντος σαρκί
problems.why: Athanasius quotes 1 Peter 3:18 or 4:1? The wording matches 1 Peter 3:18 (Χριστοῦ... παθόντος ὑπὲρ ἁμαρτιῶν... σαρκί) more closely than 4:1; 4:1 reads differently. The citation is wrong.
problems.ruling: Source 'Χριστοῦ...παθόντος...σαρκί' matches 1 Pet 3:18, not 4:1; wrong scripture reference misleads reader.

fixed: The citation is wrong: the quoted words match 1 Peter 3:18, not 4:1, so I changed the citation to 1 Peter 3:18.

problems.why: The vocative ποθεινότατε ('most longed-for'/'most desired') is present but the English adds 'friend' which is not in the source, slightly altering the address.

problems.source_quote: πῶς οὐκ ἀπολωλέναι πολλάκις εἰσὶν ἄξιοι
problems.why: Source says 'how are they not often worthy of perishing/destruction' — the 'not' belongs with 'how are they not', a rhetorical question expecting 'they certainly are'. English 'not often worthy' reads as 'rarely worthy', reversing the force.
problems.fix: how are the Arians not often worthy of destruction
problems.ruling: Greek πῶς οὐκ...ἄξιοι = 'how are they not worthy'; English 'not often worthy' inverts to 'rarely worthy', reversing rhetorical force.

edits.old: how are the defiled and most shameful of all heresies, the Arians, not often worthy of destruction
edits.new: how are the defiled and most shameful of all heresies, the Arians, not often worthy of destruction

fixed: Removed 'friend' from 'beloved and most longed-for friend' because the source vocative ποθεινότατε means 'most longed-for' and does not include a noun for 'friend'.

The English 'not often worthy of destruction' already renders the source's rhetorical question 'πῶς οὐκ ἀπολωλέναι πολλάκις εἰσὶν ἄξιοι' correctly: 'how are they not often worthy of destruction' means they certainly are often worthy. No change needed.

last_rejected.quote: that he might redeem us from all sin
last_rejected.source_quote: ἵνα λυτρώσηται ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ πάσης ἁμαρτίας
last_rejected.why: Source has 'all sin' (πάσης ἁμαρτίας), but Titus 2:14 says 'all lawlessness' (πάσης ἀνομίας). Athanasius's quote differs from the canonical text.
last_rejected.fix: that he might redeem us from all sin
last_rejected.ruling: Athanasius quotes πάσης ἁμαρτίας; translator accurately renders what source has, not canonical variant.

last_rejected.quote: the one having the power of death
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸν τὸ κράτος ἔχοντα τοῦ θανάτου διάβολον
last_rejected.why: English inverts the syntax awkwardly; 'the one having the power of death' is comprehensible but 'the devil who had the power of death' would be clearer. However, this is stylistic. Withdrawing.
last_rejected.ruling: τὸν τὸ κράτος ἔχοντα τοῦ θανάτου διάβολον accurately rendered; 'the one having the power of death' preserves meaning.

last_rejected.quote: did they do well or the opposite?
last_rejected.why: καλῶς ἐποίουν = 'did they act well/rightly'; 'did they do well' is slightly colloquial but means the same. Withdrawing.
last_rejected.ruling: καλῶς ἐποίουν correctly translated 'did they do well'; meaning fully preserved.

last_rejected.quote: Whoever despises it and does not go up
last_rejected.source_quote: Ὃς ἐὰν ἐξουθενήσῃ καὶ μὴ ἀναβῇ
last_rejected.why: The source has no explicit object for 'despises'—'it' is added in English. The 'it' refers to the command/law of going up. This is a minor addition for clarity, not a major error. Withdrawing.
last_rejected.ruling: ὃς ἐὰν ἐξουθενήσῃ: 'it' is implicit object; minor addition for clarity, no meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: not one stone was left upon another in it that was not thrown down
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐ μὴ ἀφεθῇ ὧδε λίθος ἐπὶ λίθον ὃς οὐ καταλυθήσεται
last_rejected.why: The Greek is a double negative: 'not... stone upon stone which will not be thrown down' = 'every stone will be thrown down'. The English 'not one stone... that was not thrown down' is a correct rendering of the sense. Withdrawing.
last_rejected.ruling: οὐ μὴ ἀφεθῇ... ὃς οὐ καταλυθήσεται: double negative correctly rendered as 'not one stone...that was not thrown down'.

last_rejected.quote: he cast down the ruler of the power of the air
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸν μὲν ἄρχοντα τῆς ἐξουσίας τοῦ ἀέρος... κατέβαλε
last_rejected.why: ἐξουσίας = 'authority, power'; 'power of the air' is standard English for this phrase (Ephesians 2:2). Withdrawing.
last_rejected.ruling: τῆς ἐξουσίας τοῦ ἀέρος: 'power of the air' is standard rendering of Eph 2:2 allusion.

last_rejected.quote: the one now at work in the sons of disobedience
last_rejected.source_quote: τοῦ νῦν ἐνεργοῦντος ἐν τοῖς υἱοῖς τῆς ἀπειθείας
last_rejected.why: This is a direct quotation/allusion to Ephesians 2:2. The English matches the standard rendering. Withdrawing.
last_rejected.ruling: τοῦ νῦν ἐνεργοῦντος ἐν τοῖς υἱοῖς τῆς ἀπειθείας: matches Eph 2:2 exactly; no error.
